analysis:
Examined the two base-text units of MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 530-1552), with the patch excerpt used to orient on the head changes. The PR appears to add Flint model handling: rawFlintControls.invalid at line 327, FlintAnswerStopConstraint stream filter, engineStopStrings disabled for modelType flint, answerStopFilter and withholdReasoning plumbing into makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream and makeEventStream, and a reworked early-cancel/terminal path. The patch excerpt is truncated and the head text is not supplied, so most of the head logic (the Flint filter, the withholdReasoning policy, and the changes at head lines 1205-1210, 1272-1278, 1382-1391 and 1427-1450) could not be reviewed directly.

Observed base behavior for context: the media path reserves memory through mediaGate and releases it on every exit. Fail-closed handling remains for media on a non-VLM model (mediaUnsupportedByModel), for missing bridges, and for tool-choice enforcement. Prefix-cache scope still flows from the coordinator-authored requestCacheScope into cacheScope, and the native MiMo media path sets cacheEnabled:false. Neither is changed in the visible excerpt (T-041, A-001).

Remaining questions for deeper review, none of which is a supported finding:
1. Whether disabling engine-side stop strings for Flint and filtering at the stream layer correctly stops generation (T-010, resource exhaustion) and does not leak post-stop text.
2. Whether withholding reasoning for Flint cannot leak reasoning content into the visible stream on error or terminal paths.
3. Whether the changed release and cancel ordering at head lines 1205-1210 and 1445-1450 still fires releaseBox and cancelUpstream on every path, so no model pin, KV reservation or native lease leaks (availability).
4. Whether the new Flint paths still pass cacheScope unchanged.

No concrete security regression is supported by the visible evidence.
